r-0001.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
r-0001.notes: The rule covers residential dwelling units in Berkeley with no building-level limits. The exemptions are product-based (aggregated anonymous data publishers, affordable housing limit-setting tools, market research or software testing tools). They do not turn on building characteristics, so no tests are written for them. Rent Ordinance coverage and exemption criteria from related records are not incorporated here because ch. 13.63 does not reference them.

r-0002.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees (BMC 13.78.010)
r-0002.notes: Coverage is any owner or agent charging a screening fee for residential rental property in Berkeley. No building-level limits or exemptions are stated, so there are no tests. The fee-charging condition is the trigger for the rule, not a building attribute.

r-0003.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
r-0003.notes: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements (BMC 13.78.018), with no building-level limits. The Cal. Civ. Code 1950.6 screening-fee carve-out concerns the type of fee, not the building, so no test is needed. Rent Ordinance exemptions in related records are not stated for this rule.

r-0004.title: Berkeley just cause eviction rules as amended by Measure BB

tests.source_text: university rental units such as dormitories
tests.note: Dormitories and university rental units are exempt; apartments pass.

tests.source_text: owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started
tests.note: Shared-kitchen/bath exemption depends on the landlord's residence at the start of the tenancy, which the data cannot see. Engine should answer unknown.

tests.source_text: Exempt: 'Golden Duplex'
tests.note: Golden Duplex is a duplex owner-occupied on Dec 31, 1979 and currently; the data cannot see owner occupancy. A duplex is needed for it to be possible.

tests.source_text: tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied
tests.note: Depends on ADU presence, owner occupancy and tenancy start date, which the data cannot see. Engine should answer unknown.

tests.source_text: nonprofit cooperatives
tests.note: Ownership structure is not visible in the data.

r-0004.notes: Both fully and partially covered units are subject to just cause, so there is no year_built or certificate-of-occupancy limit; the build-date and tenancy-date distinctions only change the coverage category. Only the listed exemptions limit coverage. Owner-move-in and Ellis Act text describes eviction grounds, not coverage, so it is not turned into a test.

r-0005.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA), Rent Board Regulation 1148

tests.source_text: new construction built and issued a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980 ... Not rent controlled
tests.note: New construction with a CO after June 1980 is not rent controlled and is outside the AGA. D009 gives only month and year, so the cutoff is approximated as 1980-06-01. Fully covered units are described as most multifamily buildings built before 1980.

tests.source_text: Not rent controlled: ... most condominiums
tests.note: Most condominiums are not rent controlled.

tests.source_text: university rental units such as dormitories; nonprofit cooperatives
tests.note: Dormitories and university rental units are exempt from the ordinance.

r-0005.notes: Coverage is taken from the related D006/D009 descriptions of fully covered units. Owner-specific exemptions (Golden Duplex, owner sharing kitchen or bath, ADU with owner-occupant) and the AGA eligibility conditions (registration fees, repairs, deposit interest) depend on facts the data cannot show, so they are not encoded. The Costa-Hawkins carve-out for tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01 is not testable from the data.
r-0005.review_ruling: instructions/rulings_05.md #2: tenancy length is a tenant-level fact that decides when an increase may be taken, not whether the building is covered. Drop the tenancy_months test; keep COO 1980 cutoff, condo/single-family, dormitory/co-op and golden-duplex tests.

r-0006.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance

tests.source_text: owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence
tests.note: Owner occupancy cannot be seen in the data, so the engine cannot confirm it. The exemption only applies to 1-3 unit properties.

tests.source_text: limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties
tests.note: Subsidy status is not visible in the data. The exemption is described as limited and its scope is not detailed.

tests.source_text: units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
tests.note: Tenancy circumstances are not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9
tests.note: Lease terms are not visible in the data.

r-0006.notes: Coverage is all rental housing providers in Berkeley, with no building-level limits. Every test is an exemption the data cannot see. The lifetime sex offender exemption concerns the applicant, not the building, so it has no test.

r-0007.title: Berkeley security deposit interest coverage

tests.source_text: university rental units such as dormitories
tests.note: Dormitory/university units are exempt; an apartment building passes.

tests.source_text: Exempt: 'Golden Duplex'
tests.note: Golden Duplex exemption depends on owner occupancy on Dec 31, 1979 and currently; the data cannot see this. A duplex is the only possible case.

tests.source_text: nonprofit cooperatives
tests.note: Nonprofit cooperative status is not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: owner shares kitchen or bath with tenant if owner lived on the property when the tenancy started
tests.note: Owner-occupancy and shared facilities are not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 on properties where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied
tests.note: ADU and owner-occupancy status are not visible in the data.

r-0007.notes: Coverage is stated as fully or partially covered units (multifamily pre-1980, post-1980 new construction, single-family, most condos, certain subsidized units), which together span nearly all residential types. This gives no building-level limit, and the 'covered by the Rent Ordinance' wording is circular, so no coverage test is written. Only the exemptions become tests.

r-0008.title: [notice-only] Boston Housing Stability Notification Act

tests.source_text: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
tests.note: Institutional/care facility exclusion; apartment buildings pass.

r-0008.notes: Notice-only ordinance covering all rental units in Boston except the listed institutional facilities. No unit-count, age, or owner-type limits are stated.

r-0011.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (criminal history)

tests.value: DND funding/land or BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units
tests.source_text: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy
tests.note: Coverage depends on public funding or income-restricted status, which the data cannot show; not a general private-market rule.

r-0011.notes: Applies only via DND funding/land or BPDA IDP income-restricted units (and the Affirmative Marketing Program). Exemptions for direct relationship/unreasonable risk, current criminal behavior, and preemption by conflicting federal or state requirements are applicant- or case-specific and not building-level, so no tests were written for them.

r-0012.title: Boston fair housing protection for renters using rental assistance
r-0012.notes: Coverage is housing in the City of Boston with no stated exemptions and no building-level limits. The 'renters and applicants using rental assistance' condition describes the protected class, not a building characteristic, so no test is written for it. The related records' exemptions belong to other rules (just-cause notice and the DND-funded Fair Chance policy) and do not describe who is covered by or exempt from this rule.

r-0013.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
r-0013.notes: General antitrust rule that covers any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm, not limited to housing. Its only exemptions are end consumers and single-firm algorithms that use only the business's own data. Neither exemption depends on a building-level fact, so no building tests apply.

r-0014.title: California application screening fee cap and conditions (Civ. Code § 1950.6)
r-0014.notes: The rule covers any landlord or agent charging a screening fee to an applicant for residential rental housing. No building-level limits are stated. The only exemption is non-preemption of federal or state housing assistance program rules on deposits and fees. That is not a building-level test and is not tied to anything the data can see, so no test is written for it.

r-0015.title: California Tenant Protection Act - just cause for termination

tests.source_text: Transient/tourist hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended-care and licensed care facilities; school dormitories
tests.note: Excluded institutional and transient categories.

tests.source_text: housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years
tests.note: New construction exempt for 15 years; year_built used as proxy with cutoff year treated as unknown.

tests.source_text: Tenant has occupied for 12 months (or 24 months if an additional adult tenant was added before an existing tenant reached 24 months)
tests.note: Tenancy length is not visible in the data; protection attaches only after 12 months (24 in the added-tenant case).

tests.source_text: owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; shared bathroom/kitchen with owner-occupant; separately alienable property not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, with written exemption notice
tests.note: Owner identity and occupancy are not visible. The separately alienable property exemption also requires written notice to the tenant. Multi-unit apartment buildings are not exempt on this basis.

tests.source_text: deed-restricted affordable housing
tests.note: Deed restriction or subsidy status is not visible in the data.

r-0015.notes: Mobilehome owners are also exempt. Not applicable where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 2019-09-01, or a later more protective one, covers the property. The section is repealed 2030-01-01. Query date 2026-10-01.

r-0016.title: Statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act), Civ. Code § 1947.12

tests.source_text: The cap does not apply to housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome).
tests.note: Rolling 15-year new-construction exemption; the engine uses year_built as a proxy for the certificate-of-occupancy date.

tests.source_text: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing
tests.note: Deed-restricted or subsidized housing is exempt. The engine cannot see subsidy status, so this is unknown.

tests.source_text: dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school
tests.note: Only dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school are exempt.

tests.source_text: separately alienable property (e.g. single-family homes, condos) whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member, and where the required written exemption notice was given
tests.note: The single-family or condo exemption depends on the owner type and on the written notice. The engine cannot see either, so this is unknown. Multi-unit apartment buildings are not separately alienable, so the exception cannot apply to them.

tests.source_text: a duplex in which the owner occupies one unit as a principal residence
tests.note: The duplex owner-occupancy exemption cannot be seen by the engine. It is impossible for buildings that are not duplexes.

r-0016.notes: The statewide cap applies to residential property older than 15 years, using year_built as a proxy for the certificate-of-occupancy date. Exemptions for local rent control stricter than the state cap, mobilehome homeowners, and the two-unit owner-occupied case are not visible in the address data. Date limits (March 15, 2019 and February 18, 2021 for mobilehomes) are look-back application dates, not building-level tests. The statute is repealed as of 2030-01-01, after the query date.

r-0017.title: Criminal history screening limits (Civil Rights Council regulations)
r-0017.notes: Coverage is housing decisions by landlords in California using criminal history information, with no building-level limits and no exemptions stated. Related records describe other rules' exemptions (e.g. owner-occupied or small-landlord carve-outs for other rules), which do not state exemptions for this rule's category, so none are applied.

r-0018.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban and subsidy-tenant credit/income screening limits (FEHA)
r-0018.notes: The rule covers owners of any housing accommodation under FEHA, with no building-level limits. The subsidy-specific credit and income rules apply only where a government rent subsidy exists, which the data cannot see. Exemptions for asking about income level or source, and for verifying employment, references and identity, describe permitted conduct and are not building-level exclusions. The owner-occupied room-rental exception from the FAQ is uncertain for source of income and is not encoded as a test.

r-0019.title: California residential security deposit cap and return rules (Civ. Code § 1950.5)

tests.source_text: The two-month cap applies if the landlord is a natural person or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
tests.note: This only governs whether the 2-month small-landlord cap applies instead of the 1-month cap. The base 1-month cap covers all residential rentals. The engine cannot see owner identity, so this is unknown for the small-landlord tier.

r-0019.notes: The base rule (one-month cap, 21-day return, no 'nonrefundable' label) covers all residential dwelling rentals. The only building-level fact tied to the small-landlord tier is the four-unit ceiling, so a building with more than 4 units cannot qualify for the 2-month tier. The service-member, six-month-advance-payment and pre-July-1-2024 exemptions are tenancy- or transaction-specific and are not visible to the engine.

r-0020.title: Cambridge policy order initiating ban on algorithmic rent-setting services
r-0020.notes: The policy order covers residential property managers in general. The 'large or corporate' wording is descriptive and gives no numeric or building-level limit. No exemptions are stated. The exemptions in the related records belong to other rules (tenant rights notification, fair housing) and do not describe this rule's category, so they are not applied. The measure is only a proposal and not enacted law.

r-0021.title: [notice-only] Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance (Cambridge M.C. ch. 8.71)

tests.source_text: Rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, or in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term assistance, treatment or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse; Short Term Rental Units under Cambridge Zoning Ordinance Art. 4, Sec. 4.60.
tests.note: Excludes institutional/care facilities and short-term rental units; an ordinary apartment building passes.

r-0021.notes: Notice-only ordinance applying to residential rental agreements generally (including a single dwelling unit and tenants at will). The only limits are the facility and short-term-rental exemptions. No unit-count, age, or owner-type limits are stated.

r-0022.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance: source-of-income protection (incl. Section 8)

tests.source_text: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
tests.note: Exemption applies only to owner-occupied 2-family dwellings; the engine cannot see owner occupancy, so owner_type is checked and is unknown at address level. Duplexes may be exempt if the owner lives there.

r-0022.notes: Rule covers all rental housing transactions in Cambridge except owner-occupied 2-family dwellings. Owner occupancy is not visible to the engine. Buildings that are not 2-family (units != 2, or building_type not duplex) cannot qualify for the exemption. Ordinance text itself is not in the corpus; only a secondary summary.

r-0023.title: Algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing market prohibited

tests.source_text: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
tests.note: Medical, long-term care and detention facilities are not residential dwelling units; apartments and other housing pass.

r-0023.notes: Coverage is any primary residence in Hoboken, so there are no unit-count, age or ownership limits. The only building-level limit is the exclusion of medical, long-term care and detention facilities. The NJ FAIR Act preemption is not modeled.

r-0024.title: Proposed Hoboken ordinance prohibiting algorithmic rent-fixing

tests.source_text: Medical, long-term care, or detention facilities.
tests.note: Medical, long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.

r-0024.notes: Coverage is all residential rental units in Hoboken, with only the facility-type exemption. The 365-day nonpublic competitor information definition is not a building-level limit. Preemption by the NJ FAIR Act is not modeled.

r-0025.title: Mandatory disclosures for rental increases over 10%
r-0025.notes: Applies to all residential landlords raising rent by more than 10% on renewal for a current tenant. No building-level limits or exemptions stated. The 10% increase threshold is a trigger for the duty, not a building attribute, so no test is added.

r-0026.title: Hoboken Rent Control: annual rent increase cap (§ 155-5)

tests.source_text: Motels and hotels
tests.note: Hotels and motels are exempt from rent control.

tests.source_text: multiple dwellings built after June 25, 1987 for the lesser of mortgage amortization or 30 years (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1)
tests.note: The exemption depends on the mortgage amortization term and statutory filings that the data cannot show. A newer building is therefore unknown, not excluded. year_built is the proxy.

tests.source_text: school-owned student housing; government-owned housing
tests.note: Owner identity is not in the data, so the result is unknown.

r-0026.notes: Exemptions for newly constructed dwellings on first rental, buildings vacant since 1984, industrial/commercial property, and condo/co-op owner-occupant decontrol depend on facts the data cannot see and are not turned into tests. Preemption by a government rent-regulating agency is likewise not tested. The 10% disclosure record and the algorithmic rent-setting records are different rules and were not used.

r-0027.title: Preventing Algorithmic Rent-Fixing in the Rental Housing Market (Ord. 25-057, § 218-12)

tests.source_text: residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities
tests.note: Excludes institutional facilities that are not residential dwelling units.

tests.source_text: licensed real estate agents operating in accordance with state regulations
tests.note: Agent exemption depends on the actor's licensing status, which is not visible in the address data. It does not limit building coverage.

r-0027.notes: The ban concerns conduct by lessors and service providers rather than building characteristics. The exemption for owners of multiple properties applies only to actions related exclusively to properties under the same owner. The rent-control 1-4 unit exemption is not used because it describes a different rule category. The ordinance's preemption by the NJ FAIR Act is not addressed.

r-0028.title: Jersey City ban on rent-setting algorithms (RealPage-type software)

tests.source_text: residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional faci
tests.note: Related Ord. 25-057 record excludes these non-residential settings from 'residential dwelling units'.

tests.source_text: real estate agents were excluded at the sponsor's agreement
tests.note: Agent exclusion depends on the actor's identity, which the data cannot show; applies to the actor rather than the building.

r-0028.notes: Ordinance text not in the article; coverage per related Ord. 25-057 record: residential dwelling units (primary residences). The multi-property owner exemption applies only to actions within the same owner's properties and is not building-visible, so no test was added. The 1-4 unit exemption in the rent control record is specific to that rule and was not applied here.

r-0029.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Municipal Code Chapter 260)

tests.source_text: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt from rent control
tests.note: Properties with 1-4 units are exempt, so only buildings with 5 or more units are covered. Owners may request other permitted exemptions, but their criteria are not stated.

r-0029.notes: The only building-level limit stated is the exemption for 1-4 unit properties. Other permitted exemptions under Ch. 260 are not listed on the page, so none are tested.

r-0030.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)

tests.source_text: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, ... some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance-abuse treatment centers
tests.note: Excluded non-residential or institutional categories; an apartment building passes this test.

tests.source_text: Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
tests.note: Tenancy length is not visible in the data, so the engine cannot confirm it.

tests.source_text: certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities ... some HACLA or government-owned properties
tests.note: Owner identity and the owner's roommate exemption are not visible in the data.

r-0030.notes: The JCO covers most residential properties not regulated by the RSO. The RSO covers buildings first built on or before October 1, 1978, so the JCO applies to buildings with a certificate of occupancy after that date, per the related rent_increase_limits record. Single-family dwellings are covered, so no building_type exclusion is added for them. RSO-covered units are excluded here and have their own just cause rules.

r-0031.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO

tests.source_text: Residential hotels as defined in Health & Safety Code § 50519 and LAMC § 47.70 et seq. (§ 151.22).
tests.note: Residential/transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses excluded from coverage; apartments pass.

tests.source_text: No relocation payment when evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager
tests.note: Depends on eviction facts and tenancy type the data cannot see; cannot be determined from address data.

r-0031.notes: Coverage is RSO units (built on or before Oct 1, 1978) plus JCO units (most other residential, including newer buildings and single-family), so effectively most residential rentals. No year cutoff is applied because the JCO covers non-RSO units. Exemptions for natural-disaster hazards, government orders and the Mom & Pop reduced amounts depend on eviction-specific facts not in the data.

r-0032.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) allowable rent increases

tests.source_text: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978; Exempt from the RSO: certificate of occupancy first issued after October 1, 1978
tests.note: Certificate-of-occupancy cutoff; year_built is only a proxy.

tests.source_text: One-family dwellings are exempt unless two or more dwelling units are on the same parcel (duplexes and condominiums are not excepted).
tests.note: Single-family parcels with one dwelling are exempt. Duplexes and condos remain covered.

r-0032.notes: Hotel/motel exemption is already covered by occupancy rules for stays over 30 days. Condo/townhome tenancies commenced after 1995 are exempt from rent regulation, but that depends on tenancy start date, which the data cannot show; no test is added because it is not representable by the fields. Luxury housing certification, government-regulated housing and 55-year affordable agreements depend on facts not in the data.

r-0033.title: LAMC Sec. 45.67 Prohibited Activities (source-of-income discrimination)
r-0033.notes: Coverage is any person offering, renting, or listing any housing accommodation in the City of Los Angeles, and no exemptions are stated, so there are no building-level limits.

r-0034.title: LA payment of interest on security deposits (LAMC § 151.06.02)

tests.source_text: Landlords subject to Civil Code § 1950.5 with RSO tenants; Properties within the City of Los Angeles subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LARSO)
tests.note: RSO coverage cutoff from related rent-increase record: rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978.

tests.source_text: Does not govern mobile home parks.

r-0034.notes: Coverage is limited to RSO-covered units, so the RSO cutoff of October 1, 1978 is used. The deposit-held-for-one-year condition depends on facts the data cannot show and is not tested.

r-0035.title: H.5222 - An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
r-0035.notes: H.5222 is a pending bill and the capture is a status page only. It does not reproduce the bill text, and no coverage or exemption language is stated here or in the related records. Scope must be checked in the bill itself, so the engine should answer unknown.

r-0036.title: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting (S.2983)
r-0036.notes: The page gives only the bill title and committee history, so the operative scope, definitions and exemptions are not in the corpus. The related record H.5222 also lists no coverage or exemptions. The bill is pending and not enacted, so the engine should answer unknown rather than applies.

r-0037.title: Rental broker fees payable only by the party who engaged the broker
r-0037.notes: Coverage is defined by who acts (licensed brokers or salespersons finding rental dwellings for a fee), not by building characteristics. No building-level limits or exemptions are stated, so there are no tests.

r-0040.title: Source-of-income / housing subsidy discrimination ban (M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10))
r-0040.notes: The ban applies to any person furnishing rental accommodations, and no building-level limits or exemptions are stated. The 100-day vacation-rental exclusion in the related security deposit record belongs to c. 186 § 15B and not to this rule, so no test was written for it.

r-0041.title: Massachusetts security deposit limits and handling (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B)

tests.value: tenancy longer than 100 days or not for vacation/recreational purpose
tests.source_text: does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of one hundred days or less in duration which is for a vacation or recreational purpose
tests.note: Short-term (100 days or less) vacation or recreational rentals are exempt. The engine cannot see rental duration or purpose, so this is not checkable from address data.

r-0041.notes: Statewide statute covering residential leases and tenancies-at-will, with no building-type, unit-count, age, or owner limits. The only exemption is short-term vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less, which is a use fact not visible in address data.

r-0042.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act

tests.source_text: Residential dwelling unit excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.
tests.note: Excludes inpatient medical, licensed long-term care, and detention/correctional facilities; an ordinary apartment building passes.

r-0042.notes: The act covers owners of one or more rental residential dwelling units, so there is no unit-count or age limit. The software and algorithm exemptions (human-analysis spreadsheets, public rent estimators, listing databases, government affordability programs) concern the tool used, not the building, and cannot be tested from address facts. Not yet effective: the effective date is 2027-07-01, after the 2026-10-01 query date.

r-0043.title: Residential rental application fee cap (P.L. 2025, c.405)

tests.source_text: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent
tests.note: Exemption for one-family and two-family dwellings. Single_family and duplex are used as proxies for these. Units in larger buildings are covered.

tests.source_text: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent
tests.note: A building with one or two units is exempt. Only buildings with 3 or more units are covered.

tests.source_text: New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees, unless the licensee is the landlord of the property
tests.note: Concerns the identity and licensing of the person charging the fee. It cannot be seen at the address level.

r-0043.notes: Rule in force since 2026-05-01. The $50 cap applies to residential rentals other than one- or two-family dwellings. The licensee exemption depends on who charges the fee and cannot be determined from address data.

r-0044.title: CORI housing screening limits (803 CMR 5.00)
r-0044.notes: The rule covers requestors (landlords, agents, housing authorities, property managers) who screen rental applicants. It states no building-level limits such as year built, unit count or building type. The exemptions describe which CORI access level applies and what a landlord may do, not which buildings are exempt. So no tests are needed.

r-0045.title: Source-of-income / housing subsidy discrimination ban (M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10))
r-0045.notes: Coverage is any person furnishing rental accommodations; the page states no exemptions and no building-level limits, so no tests are needed.

r-0047.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act

tests.source_text: Residential dwelling unit excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.
tests.note: Assessor use categories for inpatient medical, long-term care and detention/correctional facilities are excluded; apartments pass.

r-0047.notes: The other exemptions (spreadsheets without AI, databases that only query unprocessed data, public rent estimates, brokerage databases, government affordability programs) concern tools and programs rather than building characteristics, so they get no building-level tests. The act is not effective until 2027-07-01, which is after the 2026-10-01 query date.

r-0048.title: Residential rental application fee cap (P.L. 2025, c.405)

tests.source_text: Dwelling units in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent
tests.note: One- and two-family dwellings are exempt, so the rule applies only to buildings with more than 2 units.

tests.source_text: New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees, unless the licensee is the landlord of the property
tests.note: The data cannot show whether the applicant fee is charged by a licensee acting as agent rather than as landlord.

r-0048.notes: Effective 2026-05-01, in force at the query date. Cap is $50, adjusted for CPI starting in 2027. The one- and two-family exemption is expressed as a units > 2 test. The licensee exemption cannot be seen in the data.

r-0049.title: Anti-Eviction Act (good cause required)

tests.source_text: does not apply to hotel or motel guests or guest houses rented to transient or seasonal tenants
tests.note: Transient/seasonal hotel, motel and guest house occupancy is excluded; apartments pass.

tests.source_text: May not apply to owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units
tests.note: Owner occupancy cannot be seen in the data; the exemption only applies to premises with two or fewer rental units, so larger buildings are not exempt.

tests.source_text: does not apply to a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it
tests.note: Trust or family occupancy cannot be seen in the data; it is a narrow exemption for a single unit.

r-0049.notes: Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are covered by a separate section (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2) with narrower grounds, so the full good-cause list does not apply to them. Owner occupancy is not in the data, so those cases are unknown.

r-0050.title: Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required for lease non-renewal

tests.source_text: motels or hotels, and transient or seasonal units
tests.note: Hotels, motels and transient/seasonal occupancy are excluded; an apartment building passes.

tests.source_text: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (which have a separate section)
tests.note: Owner occupancy cannot be seen in the data. The exemption only applies to buildings with 2-3 units, so buildings with more than 3 units or only 1 unit cannot qualify.

r-0050.notes: Coverage is residential rentals generally. Exclusions are hotels/motels/transient/seasonal units and owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (which have their own section). No effective date is given, and the good causes are in later parts of the guide.

r-0051.title: Newark Ban the Box - Housing (criminal record check practices)

tests.source_text: excludes (1) a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit
tests.note: Owner occupancy of the other unit in a two-family dwelling is not visible in the data. A duplex is the only building type where this exclusion could apply.

tests.source_text: a room or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling
tests.note: Owner occupancy of a one-family dwelling is not visible in the data. This exclusion could only apply to single-family buildings.

tests.source_text: property designated for a government program that encourages housing for people with criminal histories
tests.note: Program designation is not visible in the data.

r-0051.notes: The two owner-occupancy exclusions are encoded separately, each defeated when the building type rules it out. The exemption for cases where federal or state law requires or permits consideration of criminal history is not an address-level fact, so no test is written for it. The related rent control record gives no coverage criteria for this rule.

r-0052.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income / rent payment protection

tests.source_text: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling
tests.note: Exemption applies only to owner-occupied two-family dwellings (one unit rented) and rooms in owner-occupied one-family homes. Owner occupancy is not visible in the data. The exemption is impossible in buildings with more than 2 units that are not single-family or duplex.

r-0052.notes: Source-of-income protection covers all rental property. The only building-level carve-out is the owner-occupied two-family unit and rooms in an owner-occupied one-family home. Religious-organization preference and housing for older persons relate to other protected classes (religion, familial status), not source of income, so no tests are added for them.

r-0053.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act (criminal record screening limits)

tests.source_text: other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
tests.note: Owner-occupied premises with four or fewer units are excluded. The data cannot show owner occupancy, so this is unknown unless the building has more than four units.

r-0053.notes: The only building-level limit is the owner-occupied premises of not more than four units exclusion. The provisions on federally assisted housing and sex offender registration status concern what screening is allowed, not coverage, so they get no test.

r-0054.title: NJ Security Deposit Law: cap of 1.5 months' rent

tests.source_text: Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units are excluded unless the tenant gives the landlord 30 days written notice invoking the act.
tests.note: Owner occupancy and the tenant's written notice are not visible in the data. The exemption only applies to premises with two or fewer rental units, so the result is unknown for those and the test is defeated for buildings with more than 2 units.

tests.source_text: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (a tenant there may opt in 30 days after a written request to the landlord).
tests.note: Owner occupancy cannot be determined from the data. Buildings with 4 or more units cannot qualify for this exemption.

r-0054.notes: Seasonal rentals of up to 125 days only exempt the interest-account rules, not the whole rule, so no test is added for them. Mobile homes and other dwellings are covered. Pet deposit and first-month-rent details are requirements, not coverage limits.

r-0055.title: Newark Rent Control: annual CPI-based rent increase cap

tests.source_text: hotel/motel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space
tests.note: Hotel/motel/transient and commercial space are exempt; apartments pass.

tests.source_text: newly constructed multiple dwellings ... The period is the amortization period of the initial mortgage or 30 years after completion of construction, whichever is less.
tests.note: New construction exemption lasts the lesser of mortgage amortization or 30 years and depends on facts not in the data, so a newer building is unknown rather than excluded.

tests.source_text: public housing; ... units under a contract with a governmental agency that regulates rent
tests.note: Public housing, rehabilitated Section 8 units and units under a governmental rent-regulating contract are exempt; subsidy status is not visible in the data.

r-0055.notes: Coverage is limited to multiple dwellings as defined in 19:2-2 (the definition is not in this capture, so no unit-count test is written). Vacant-dwelling exemption (19:2-18.2) is not in this part and is not testable.

r-0056.title: Newark Ban the Box - Housing (criminal record check practices)

tests.source_text: excludes ... (2) a room or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling
tests.note: Exclusion applies only when the owner occupies the one-family dwelling; owner occupancy is not visible, so the test is unknown for single-family addresses.

tests.source_text: excludes (1) a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit
tests.note: Owner occupancy is not visible in the data. Defeated when the building is not a duplex.

r-0056.notes: Covers rentals by landlords and brokers. Owner-occupancy exclusions apply to two-family and one-family dwellings, which the data cannot confirm. The government-program and law-required exemptions depend on facts not in the data and are not building-level tests.

r-0057.title: San Diego Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price Fixing (SDMC §98.1103)
r-0057.notes: The rule covers all residential rental property in the City of San Diego. The exemptions apply to types of software (aggregated historical reports, affordable-housing program rent-setting tools, appraisal software), not to buildings. The engine cannot test them from address data, so no building-level tests are written. The just-cause exemptions in the related records are for a different rule and were not used.

r-0058.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause for termination of tenancy)

tests.source_text: Transient/tourist hotels; mobilehomes subject to the MRL; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care or licensed elder care and nonprofit transitional housing; school-owned dormitories
tests.note: Excluded non-residential-style or institutional occupancies.

tests.source_text: Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years is exempt (unless a mobilehome)
tests.note: Certificate of occupancy date approximated via year_built.

tests.source_text: owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex
tests.note: Owner occupancy is not visible in the data; the exemption applies only to single-family or duplex buildings, so larger buildings are not affected.

tests.source_text: Separately alienable property is exempt only if the landlord is not a REIT, a corporation, an LLC with a corporate member... and the tenant received the required written exemption notice
tests.note: The condo or single-family exemption depends on owner identity and written notice, which the data cannot show.

tests.source_text: deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (but not Section 8)
tests.note: Subsidy status is not visible in the data.

r-0058.notes: Tenancy longer than 30 days is a general scope condition that the data cannot test. Shared-facility rentals with the owner are not testable.

r-0059.title: San Diego Prohibition of Discrimination Based on a Tenant's Source of Income

tests.source_text: Does not apply where the owner or a family member resides in the same residential building and shares a bathroom or kitchen facility with the tenant or prospective tenant (§98.0804)
tests.note: Shared-facility owner-occupancy exemption depends on owner residence and facility sharing, which the data cannot show.

r-0059.notes: Coverage is defined by reference to Municipal Code section 98.0720, which is not in the corpus, so coverage is incomplete. The shared-facility exemption is limited to owner or family residence in the same building; the defeated_if units > 4 is a heuristic, since large buildings rarely involve shared bathroom or kitchen with the owner. The program-compliance exception is act-specific and not a building-level test.

r-0060.title: S.F. Rent Ordinance Section 37.10C - Prohibition on Algorithmic Rent-Setting Devices
r-0060.notes: Coverage is all residential units in San Francisco. No building-level limits or exemptions are stated. The definition of 'algorithmic device' describes the software, not the building, so it adds no test.

r-0061.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9(a))
r-0061.notes: Coverage is limited to units covered by the Rent Ordinance, and the corpus does not state the ordinance's coverage criteria (for example, the 1979 certificate of occupancy cutoff applies only to rent increase limits, not to just cause). The phrase "newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979" describes units that are still covered by just cause even though they are exempt from rent limits. That is an inclusion, so it gets no exclusion test. The D082 exemption for temporary capital improvement evictions of under 20 days concerns relocation payments, not building coverage, so no test is written for it. The rule's coverage is therefore not determinable from the corpus.
r-0061.explanation_note: statutory exemptions (certain owner-occupied shared units, institutional housing) not testable from county data
r-0061.review_ruling: instructions/rulings_05.md #1: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9 just-cause protection extends to units regardless of construction date; D079 states inclusions, not exclusions. Treat coverage as all residential rental units in SF. Remaining statutory exemptions are not testable from parcel data and rare in a 5+ unit sample.

r-0062.title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase (3/1/2026\u20132/28/2027)

tests.source_text: newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 [exempt from rent increase limits]
tests.note: Related just-cause record says units with a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from rent increase limits, so only units on or before that date are covered. year_built is used as a proxy.

r-0062.notes: The rule's own text only says 'rent-controlled units subject to the Rent Ordinance', which is circular. The coverage cutoff comes from the related just-cause record. Costa-Hawkins exemptions for single-family homes and condos are also mentioned there, but the record does not state them as a clear building-type test, so none is added.

r-0038.title: Broker fee payable only by the party who engaged the broker
r-0038.notes: Coverage is defined by the broker's activity (licensed brokers and salespersons finding rental residential dwellings for a fee), not by building characteristics. Exemptions: None. No building-level limits are stated, so no tests are needed.

r-0039.title: No application fees by landlords (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
r-0039.notes: The rule applies to landlords before a tenancy begins. The only exemption is for licensed brokers charging fees under 254 CMR 7, and that depends on who charges the fee, which the data cannot show, so no building-level test is written. The 100-day vacation or recreational rental exemption in c.186 s.15B(9) comes from the related security deposit record, and it depends on tenancy purpose and length, so it is not tested either.

r-0046.title: Massachusetts security deposit limits and handling (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B)

tests.source_text: does not apply to any lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of one hundred days or less in duration which is for a vacation or recreational purpose
tests.note: Short-term vacation/recreational use of 100 days or less is exempt. The data cannot show the rental purpose or duration, so this is flagged as unknown rather than excluded.

r-0046.notes: Statewide statute covering residential leases and tenancies-at-will with no building-type, unit-count or age limits. The only exemption is the vacation/recreational rental of 100 days or less, which the engine cannot see.

r-0063.title: Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
r-0063.notes: The page limits the ordinance to affordable housing decisions but gives no thresholds or building-level criteria, and no related record defines what counts as affordable housing. The engine cannot check subsidy or affordability status, and a funding test would only restate the rule's own scope. Coverage is therefore left undefined and the engine should answer unknown.

r-0064.title: SF security deposit interest rate
r-0064.notes: The rule covers residential tenancies with security deposits and states no building-level thresholds or exemptions. The phrase 'subject to San Francisco's security deposit interest rules' only restates coverage, so it is not turned into a test. The related records give no criteria specific to this rule's category.

r-0065.title: Santa Ana ordinance limiting algorithmic rent-setting software
r-0065.notes: Coverage is all residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits, with no building-level limits stated. The exemptions are about the type of software, namely tools using only public or aggregate historical data and tools for affordable housing compliance. They do not turn on any building fact the engine can check, so no tests are written. The just-cause and rent-stabilization exemptions in related records are for other rule categories and are not used here.

r-0066.title: Santa Ana Ordinance NS-3090 (automated rent price-fixing)
r-0066.notes: Coverage is all residential rental property in Santa Ana with no unit-count or building-level thresholds. The exemptions apply to the kind of pricing software used (publicly available data only, aggregate historical data, or affordable housing compliance tools). They do not describe a type of building, so they are not turned into building-level tests.

r-0067.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance

tests.source_text: Housing produced in the last 15 years
tests.note: New construction exempt for 15 years; year_built used as proxy for certificate of occupancy.

tests.source_text: deed-restricted affordable housing
tests.note: Deed restriction status is not visible in the data.

tests.source_text: hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters

r-0067.notes: Tenancy-length protection begins after 30 days but is not a building-level test. Source is a secondary press release; later amendments may not be reflected.

r-0068.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance

tests.source_text: the cap does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995
tests.note: Full-date cutoff treated as a certificate-of-occupancy cutoff; buildings constructed after Feb 1, 1995 are exempt.

r-0068.notes: The mobile home space exemption (offered for rent after January 1, 1990) is not testable with the available fields. The owner petition for fair return is a relief procedure, not a building-level exemption, so no test was written for it. The just-cause record's 15-year exemption applies to that rule and was not used.
